text:
Alex (CEO): Thanks for joining the AMA thread — quick live follow-ups from today's all-hands. Drop short questions here and we'll answer live.
Maya (Head of Product): Quick housekeeping: we'll prioritize product/market questions first, then roadmap, then org/ops.
Jordan (Growth): Will we keep the same go-to-market focus on PLG -> sales-assisted for Dedicated? Customers keep asking about trial-to-Dedicated path.
Alex (CEO): Yes — PLG remains primary. The rule of thumb: self-serve for adoption / experiments; sales-assisted for Dedicated & Private once usage and security bar are hit. We're simplifying the conversion playbooks.
Sam (VP Eng): Follow-up: what's the expected SLA uplift for Dedicated vs Hosted? customers want concrete numbers to justify migration.
Maya (Head of Product): Targeting 99.9% monthly uptime for Dedicated with latency p95 targets in the docs. We'll publish a short SLA FAQ next week.
Ravi (CTO): On the tech side, Dedicated gets reserved GPU pools + routing optimizations. For Private, customers get our private control plane + KMS integrations.
Jordan (Growth): How do we position vs cloud AI endpoints (big clouds) vs inference vendors? I need a 1-liner for sales decks.
Alex (CEO): Positioning line: "Redwood: a production-first inference platform that balances latency, cost, and portability — from cloud to private deployments." Emphasize serving economics and unified runtime.
Jordan (Growth): Nice. Can we call out the fallback routing & cost controls as a differentiator in the deck?
Maya (Head of Product): Yes — examples: automated model fallbacks, batching/caching suggestions, and per-token cost breakdowns in Console. Those resonate in demos.
Sam (VP Eng): Competitors question: if customers ask about owning models vs Redwood hosted models, what's the guidance?
Alex (CEO): Owning models is fine; our bet is you shouldn't re-engineer inference. We win if we make serving predictable, cheaper, and easier regardless of model choice.
Ravi (CTO): Practically: we support pinned model versions + on-the-wire quantized variants. Customers can bring their model, we handle runtime and ops.
Jordan (Growth): Pricing talk — any plans to change unit economics? Heard feedback on embeddings costs for high-volume apps.
Maya (Head of Product): We're exploring volume discounts and a new embeddings tier that separates storage & compute. No final decision yet; collecting signals.
Alex (CEO): Important note: we'll avoid surprise changes to existing customers — any pricing changes will be opt-in pilot first.
Sam (VP Eng): Roadmap ask: which should ship first — optimized KV-cache for long-context or native quantized kernels for M1-like hardware?
Ravi (CTO): Short answer: long-context KV-cache wins today for customer value. Quantized kernel work is next quarter priority.
Jordan (Growth): For sales collateral, can we get a one-page comparison (Redwood vs CloudML vs InferenceX) that calls out SLA, cost controls, and deployment modes?
Maya (Head of Product): On it — I'll own a draft and share in #docs in 48 hours. Would love PM/SE feedback.
Alex (CEO): Thanks — last quick one: what metric should teams use to evaluate success for the next quarter?
Maya (Head of Product): Customer time-to-first-successful-query (TTFSQ) + cost per 1M tokens served. Those map to adoption and economics.
Jordan (Growth): Perfect. I'll update decks and outreach templates.
allhands-bot: Reminder: feedback survey link posted in #announcements. Please fill it out if you haven't. :heart:
Alex (CEO): Thanks everyone — we'll answer anything missed in follow-up threads.
